claim: Metage2Metabo (M2M) is a resource that meets the need for de novo functional screening of genome-scale metabolic networks (GSMNs) at the scale of a metagenome.
source: We present Metage2Metabo (M2M) a resource that meets the need for de novo functional screening of genome-scale metabolic networks (GSMNs) at the scale of a metagenome, and the identification of critical species with respect to metabolic cooperation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the tool's purpose.

claim: M2M comprises a flexible pipeline for the characterisation of individual metabolisms and collective metabolic complementarity.
source: M2M comprises a flexible pipeline for the characterisation of individual metabolisms and collective metabolic complementarity.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract describing the tool's capabilities.

claim: M2M identifies key species that are meaningful members of the community for functions of interest.
source: In addition, M2M identifies key species, that are meaningful members of the community for functions of interest.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a feature of the tool.

claim: M2M is applicable to collections of genomes as well as metagenome-assembled genomes.
source: We demonstrate that M2M is applicable to collections of genomes as well as metagenome-assembled genomes, permits an efficient GSMN reconstruction with Pathway Tools, and assesses the cooperation potential between species.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a demonstrated capability.

claim: M2M permits an efficient GSMN reconstruction with Pathway Tools.
source: We demonstrate that M2M is applicable to collections of genomes as well as metagenome-assembled genomes, permits an efficient GSMN reconstruction with Pathway Tools, and assesses the cooperation potential between species.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a demonstrated capability.

claim: M2M assesses the cooperation potential between species.
source: We demonstrate that M2M is applicable to collections of genomes as well as metagenome-assembled genomes, permits an efficient GSMN reconstruction with Pathway Tools, and assesses the cooperation potential between species.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a demonstrated capability.

claim: M2M identifies key organisms by reducing the complexity of a large-scale microbiota into minimal communities with equivalent properties.
source: M2M identifies key organisms by reducing the complexity of a large-scale microbiota into minimal communities with equivalent properties, suitable for further analyses.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract describing the tool's approach.

claim: Hundreds or thousands of genomes can now be reconstructed from various environments.
source: Hundreds or thousands of genomes can now be reconstructed from various environments (Pasolli et al., 2019; Forster et al., 2019; Zou et al., 2019; Stewart et al., 2018; Almeida et al., 2020), either with the help of reference genomes or through metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), paving the way for numerous downstream analyses.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Some major interactions between species occur at the metabolic level.
source: Some major interactions between species occur at the metabolic level.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Genome-scale metabolic networks (GSMNs) integrate all the expected metabolic reactions of an organism.
source: Genome-scale metabolic networks (GSMNs) integrate all the expected metabolic reactions of an organism.
evidence: This is stated as a definition in the introduction.

claim: Thiele and Palsson, 2010 defined a precise protocol for GSMN reconstruction, associating the use of automatic methods and thorough curation based on expertise, literature, and mathematical analyses.
source: Thiele and Palsson, 2010 defined a precise protocol for their reconstruction, associating the use of automatic methods and thorough curation based on expertise, literature, and mathematical analyses.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Thiele and Palsson, 2010.

claim: Pathway Tools is an all-in-one platform for GSMN reconstruction.
source: There now exists a variety of GSMN reconstruction implementations: all-in-one platforms such as Pathway Tools (Karp et al., 2016), CarveMe (Machado et al., 2018) or KBase that provides narratives from metagenomic datasets analysis up to GSMN reconstruction with ModelSEED (Henry et al., 2010; Seaver et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Karp et al., 2016.

claim: CarveMe is an all-in-one platform for GSMN reconstruction.
source: There now exists a variety of GSMN reconstruction implementations: all-in-one platforms such as Pathway Tools (Karp et al., 2016), CarveMe (Machado et al., 2018) or KBase that provides narratives from metagenomic datasets analysis up to GSMN reconstruction with ModelSEED (Henry et al., 2010; Seaver et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Machado et al., 2018.

claim: KBase provides narratives from metagenomic datasets analysis up to GSMN reconstruction with ModelSEED.
source: There now exists a variety of GSMN reconstruction implementations: all-in-one platforms such as Pathway Tools (Karp et al., 2016), CarveMe (Machado et al., 2018) or KBase that provides narratives from metagenomic datasets analysis up to GSMN reconstruction with ModelSEED (Henry et al., 2010; Seaver et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Henry et al., 2010 and Seaver et al., 2020.

claim: Reconstructed GSMNs are a resource to analyse the metabolic complementarity between species.
source: Reconstructed GSMNs are a resource to analyse the metabolic complementarity between species, which can be seen as a representation of the putative cooperation within communities (Opatovsky et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Opatovsky et al., 2018.

claim: SMETANA estimates the cooperation potential and simulates flux exchanges within communities.
source: SMETANA (Zelezniak et al., 2015) estimates the cooperation potential and simulates flux exchanges within communities.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zelezniak et al., 2015.

claim: MiSCoTo computes the metabolic potential of interacting species and performs community reduction.
source: MiSCoTo (Frioux et al., 2018) computes the metabolic potential of interacting species and performs community reduction.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Frioux et al., 2018.

claim: NetCooperate predicts the metabolic complementarity between species.
source: NetCooperate (Levy et al., 2015) predicts the metabolic complementarity between species.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Levy et al., 2015.

claim: Current constraint-based modelling tools can only be applied to communities with few members, as the computational cost scales exponentially with the number of included members.
source: However, these tools can only be applied to communities with few members, as the computational cost scales exponentially with the number of included members (Kumar et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kumar et al., 2019.

claim: Current methods require GSMNs of high quality in order to produce accurate mathematical predictions and quantitative simulations.
source: In addition, current methods require GSMNs of high quality in order to produce accurate mathematical predictions and quantitative simulations.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of current methods in the introduction.

claim: Automatic reconstruction of GSMNs scales to metagenomic datasets, but it comes with the cost of possible missing reactions and inaccurate stoichiometry that impede the use of constraint-based modelling.
source: Automatic reconstruction of GSMNs scales to metagenomic datasets, but it comes with the cost of possible missing reactions and inaccurate stoichiometry that impede the use of constraint-based modelling (Bernstein et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Bernstein et al., 2019.

claim: M2M capitalises on the parallel reconstruction of GSMNs and a relevant metabolic modelling formalism to scale to large microbiotas.
source: M2M capitalises on the parallel reconstruction of GSMNs and a relevant metabolic modelling formalism to scale to large microbiotas.
evidence: This is stated as a key feature of M2M in the introduction.

claim: M2M automates the systematic reconstruction of GSMNs using Pathway Tools or relies on GSMNs provided by the user.
source: M2M automates the systematic reconstruction of GSMNs using Pathway Tools or relies on GSMNs provided by the user.
evidence: This is stated as a feature of M2M in the introduction.

claim: The software system uses the algorithm of network expansion to capture the set of producible metabolites in a GSMN.
source: The software system uses the algorithm of network expansion (Ebenhöh et al., 2004) to capture the set of producible metabolites in a GSMN.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ebenhöh et al., 2004.

claim: The robustness of the network expansion algorithm was demonstrated by the stability of the set of reachable metabolites despite missing reactions.
source: This choice answers the needs for stoichiometry inaccuracy handling, and the robustness of the algorithm was demonstrated by the stability of the set of reachable metabolites despite missing reactions (Handorf et al., 2005; Kruse and Ebenhöh, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Handorf et al., 2005 and Kruse and Ebenhöh, 2008.

claim: M2M was applied on a collection of 1520 draft bacterial reference genomes from the gut microbiota.
source: We applied M2M on a collection of 1520 draft bacterial reference genomes from the gut microbiota (Zou et al., 2019) in order to illustrate the range of analyses the tool can produce.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zou et al., 2019 and describes the application of the tool.

claim: M2M efficiently reconstructs metabolic networks for all genomes in the gut microbiota collection.
source: This demonstrates that M2M efficiently reconstructs metabolic networks for all genomes, identifies potential metabolites produced by cooperating bacteria, and suggests minimal communities and key species associated to their production.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated result in the introduction.

claim: M2M identifies potential metabolites produced by cooperating bacteria in the gut microbiota collection.
source: This demonstrates that M2M efficiently reconstructs metabolic networks for all genomes, identifies potential metabolites produced by cooperating bacteria, and suggests minimal communities and key species associated to their production.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated result in the introduction.

claim: M2M suggests minimal communities and key species associated to metabolite production in the gut microbiota collection.
source: This demonstrates that M2M efficiently reconstructs metabolic networks for all genomes, identifies potential metabolites produced by cooperating bacteria, and suggests minimal communities and key species associated to their production.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated result in the introduction.

claim: Metabolic network reconstruction was compared between gut reference genomes and a collection of 913 cow rumen MAGs.
source: We then compared metabolic network reconstruction applied to the gut reference genomes to the results obtained with a collection of 913 cow rumen MAGs (Stewart et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Stewart et al., 2018 and describes a comparison performed.

claim: The robustness of metabolic prediction with respect to genome incompleteness was tested by degrading the rumen MAGs.
source: In addition, we tested the robustness of metabolic prediction with respect to genome incompleteness by degrading the rumen MAGs.
evidence: This describes an experiment performed to test robustness.

claim: The comparison of outputs from the pipeline indicates stability of the results with moderately degraded genomes.
source: The comparison of outputs from the pipeline indicates stability of the results with moderately degraded genomes, and the overall suitability of M2M to MAGs.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the degradation experiment.

claim: M2M is suitable for application to MAGs.
source: The comparison of outputs from the pipeline indicates stability of the results with moderately degraded genomes, and the overall suitability of M2M to MAGs.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the MAG analysis.

claim: M2M was applied to metagenomic data from 170 samples of healthy and diabetic individuals.
source: Finally, we demonstrated the applicability of M2M in practice to metagenomic data of individuals. To that purpose, we reconstructed communities for 170 samples of healthy and diabetic individuals (Forslund et al., 2015; Diener et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Forslund et al., 2015 and Diener et al., 2020.

claim: M2M can help connect sequence analyses to metabolic screening in metagenomic datasets.
source: We show how M2M can help connect sequence analyses to metabolic screening in metagenomic datasets.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated capability in the introduction.

claim: M2M's main pipeline consists in five main steps: reconstruction of metabolic networks, computation of individual metabolic capabilities, computation of collective metabolic capabilities, calculation of the cooperation potential, and identification of minimal communities and key species.
source: M2M's main pipeline (Figure 1a) consists in five main steps that can be performed sequentially or independently: (i) reconstruction of metabolic networks for all annotated genomes, (ii) computation of individual and (iii) collective metabolic capabilities, (iv) calculation of the cooperation potential, and (v) identification of minimal communities and key species for a targeted set of compounds.
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: The scope represents the metabolic potential or reachable metabolites in given nutritional conditions.
source: The scope therefore represents the metabolic potential or reachable metabolites in these conditions (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated as a definition in the Results section.

claim: Network expansion is used in the community reduction optimisation implemented in MiSCoTo.
source: Network expansion is also used in the community reduction optimisation implemented in MiSCoTo (Frioux et al., 2018), the dependency of M2M, as reduced communities are expected to produce the metabolites of interest.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Frioux et al., 2018.

claim: Key species are organisms whose GSMNs are selected in at least one of the minimal communities predicted to fulfill the metabolic objective.
source: We define as key species organisms whose GSMNs are selected in at least one of the minimal communities predicted to fulfill the metabolic objective.
evidence: This is stated as a definition in the Results section.

claim: Essential symbionts occur in every minimal community.
source: Among key species, we distinguish those that occur in every minimal community, suggesting that they possess key functions associated to the objective, from those that occur only in some communities. We call the former essential symbionts, and the latter alternative symbionts.
evidence: This is stated as a definition in the Results section.

claim: Alternative symbionts occur only in some minimal communities.
source: Among key species, we distinguish those that occur in every minimal community, suggesting that they possess key functions associated to the objective, from those that occur only in some communities. We call the former essential symbionts, and the latter alternative symbionts.
evidence: This is stated as a definition in the Results section.

claim: The gut microbiota collection contained 796 Firmicutes, 447 Bacteroidetes, 235 Actinobacteria, 36 Proteobacteria, and 6 Fusobacteria.
source: The genomes were derived from cultured bacteria, isolated from faecal samples covering typical gut phyla (Costea et al., 2018): 796 Firmicutes, 447 Bacteroidetes, 235 Actinobacteria, 36 Proteobacteria, and 6 Fusobacteria.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the dataset and supported by a citation to Costea et al., 2018.

claim: The dereplicated genomes represent 338 species.
source: The dereplicated genomes represent 338 species.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the dataset.

claim: The full M2M workflow took 155 min on a cluster with 72 CPUs and 144 Gb of memory for the gut dataset.
source: The full workflow (from GSMN reconstruction to key species computation) took 155 min on a cluster with 72 CPUs and 144 Gb of memory.
evidence: This is stated as a performance metric for the tool.

claim: A total of 3932 unique reactions and 4001 metabolites were included in the reconstructed GSMNs for the gut dataset.
source: A total of 3932 unique reactions and 4001 metabolites were included in the reconstructed GSMNs (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and presented in Table 2.

claim: The reconstructed gut metabolic networks contained on average 1144 (±255) reactions and 1366 (±262) metabolites per genome.
source: The reconstructed gut metabolic networks contained on average 1144 (±255) reactions and 1366 (±262) metabolites per genome.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the GSMN reconstruction.

claim: 74.6% of the reactions in the gut GSMNs were associated to genes.
source: Of the reactions, 74.6% were associated to genes, the remaining being spontaneous reactions or reactions added by the PathoLogic algorithm (they can be removed in M2M using the –noorphan option).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the GSMN reconstruction.

claim: The union of all individual scopes is of size 828 for the gut dataset.
source: The union of all individual scopes is of size 828 (21% of all compounds included in the GSMNs), indicating a small part of the metabolism reachable in the chosen nutritional environment (Supplementary file 1 - Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the metabolic potential analysis.

claim: 156 new metabolites were predicted as producible by the gut collection of GSMNs if cooperation is allowed.
source: Running m2m cscope predicted 156 new metabolites as producible by the gut collection of GSMNs if cooperation is allowed.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the cooperation potential analysis.

claim: 80.1% of the 156 newly producible metabolites for the gut dataset could be grouped into six categories: amino acids and derivatives, aromatic compounds, carboxy acids, coenzyme A derivatives, lipids, and sugar derivatives.
source: We analysed the composition of the 156 newly producible metabolites for the gut dataset using the ontology provided for metabolic compounds in the MetaCyc database. 80.1% of them could be grouped into six categories: amino acids and derivatives (5 metabolites), aromatic compounds (11), carboxy acids (14), coenzyme A (CoA) derivatives (10), lipids (28), sugar derivatives (58).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the analysis of cooperation potential.

claim: A total of 543 metabolic networks are predicted to be able to produce all four SCFAs (formate, acetate, propionate, and butyrate) in a cooperative context.
source: A total of 543 metabolic networks are predicted to be able to produce all four molecules in a cooperative context, 74% of them belonging the Firmicutes, as expected.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the SCFA analysis.

claim: 74% of the 543 metabolic networks predicted to produce all four SCFAs belong to Firmicutes.
source: A total of 543 metabolic networks are predicted to be able to produce all four molecules in a cooperative context, 74% of them belonging the Firmicutes, as expected.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the SCFA analysis.

claim: Predicted individual producers of the four SCFAs (n = 128) are mostly Bacteroidetes (70%).
source: Surprisingly, predicted individual producers of the four SCFAs (n = 128) are mostly Bacteroidetes (70%) suggesting the dependency of Firmicutes to interactions in order to permit the producibility of SCFAs in this experimental setting.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the SCFA analysis.

claim: The size of the minimal community is relatively small for each group of metabolites (between 4 and 11), compared to the initial community of 1520 GSMNs.
source: To our surprise, the size of the minimal community is relatively small for each group of metabolites (between 4 and 11), compared to the initial community of 1520 GSMNs.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the community reduction analysis.

claim: The number of identified key species varies between 59 and 227 for different metabolite groups.
source: The number of identified key species varies between 59 and 227, which might be closer to the total taxonomic diversity found in the human gut microbiome.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the community reduction analysis.

claim: A high proportion of key species for the production of lipids targets are Bacteroidetes.
source: In particular, essential symbionts are likely of high importance for the functions as they are found in each solution. More generally, compositions vary across the target categories: a high proportion of key species for the production of lipids targets are Bacteroidetes, whereas Firmicutes were more often key species for aminoacids and derivatives production.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the community reduction analysis.

claim: Firmicutes were more often key species for aminoacids and derivatives production.
source: In particular, essential symbionts are likely of high importance for the functions as they are found in each solution. More generally, compositions vary across the target categories: a high proportion of key species for the production of lipids targets are Bacteroidetes, whereas Firmicutes were more often key species for aminoacids and derivatives production.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the community reduction analysis.

claim: The propensity of Bacteroidetes to metabolise lipids has been proposed previously.
source: The propensity of Bacteroidetes to metabolise lipids has been proposed previously, it has for example been observed in the Bacteroides enterotype for functions related to lipolysis (Vieira-Silva et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Vieira-Silva et al., 2016.

claim: The number of optimal solutions is large, reaching more than 7 million equivalent minimal communities for the sugar-derived metabolites.
source: The number of optimal solutions is large, reaching more than 7 million equivalent minimal communities for the sugar-derived metabolites (Table 3).
evidence: This is stated in the text and presented in Table 3.

claim: The large number of optimal communities is due to combinatorial choices among a rather small number of bacteria.
source: Our analysis of key species indicates that the large number of optimal communities is due to combinatorial choices among a rather small number of bacteria (Table 3).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results presented in Table 3.

claim: Paenibacillus polymyxa, Lactobacillus lactis, Bacillus licheniformis, Lactobacillus plantarum, and Dorea longicatena are essential symbionts associated to carbohydrate-derived metabolites.
source: We further investigated the essential symbionts associated to carbohydrate-derived metabolites in our study: Paenibacillus polymyxa, Lactobacillus lactis, Bacillus licheniformis, Lactobacillus plantarum, and Dorea longicatena.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the analysis.

claim: Out of the five essential symbionts for carbohydrate-derived metabolites, the first four (Paenibacillus polymyxa, Lactobacillus lactis, Bacillus licheniformis, Lactobacillus plantarum) have already been studied in the context of probiotics.
source: Interestingly, out of these five species, the first four have already been studied in the context of probiotics, for animals or humans (Cutting, 2011; Monteagudo-Mera et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cutting, 2011 and Monteagudo-Mera et al., 2012.

claim: The study of P. polymyxa CAZymes demonstrated its ability to assist in digesting complex carbohydrates.
source: In particular, the study of P. polymyxa CAZymes demonstrated its ability to assist in digesting complex carbohydrates (Soni et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Soni et al., 2020.

claim: L. plantarum is known for its role in carbohydrate acquisition.
source: L. plantarum is also known for its role in carbohydrate acquisition (de Vries et al., 2006; Marco et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to de Vries et al., 2006 and Marco et al., 2010.

claim: Bacillus licheniformis is an essential symbiont for the lipid metabolites.
source: Bacillus licheniformis is also an essential symbiont for the lipid metabolites.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the analysis.

claim: Burkholderiales bacterium and Hungatella hathewayi occur in predictions for the lipids, carboxy acids, and aromatic metabolites.
source: Among essential symbionts for other groups of metabolites, Burkholderiales bacterium (Proteobacteria) and Hungatella hathewayi (Firmicutes) have the particularity of occurring in predictions for the lipids, carboxy acids, and aromatic metabolites.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the analysis.

claim: The Burkholderiales order's ability to degrade a variety of aromatic compounds has been established.
source: The Burkholderiales order is also poorly known, but its ability to degrade a variety of aromatic compounds has been established (Pérez-Pantoja et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Pérez-Pantoja et al., 2012.

claim: Fusobacterium varium is the only essential symbiont predicted for the coA-related metabolites.
source: Finally, the only essential symbiont predicted for the coA-related metabolites is Fusobacterium varium, a butyrate producer known for its ability to ferment both sugars and amino acids (Potrykus et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the analysis and supported by a citation to Potrykus et al., 2008.

claim: Fusobacterium varium is a butyrate producer known for its ability to ferment both sugars and amino acids.
source: Finally, the only essential symbiont predicted for the coA-related metabolites is Fusobacterium varium, a butyrate producer known for its ability to ferment both sugars and amino acids (Potrykus et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Potrykus et al., 2008.

claim: The complete M2M workflow ran in 81 min on a cluster with 72 CPUs and 144 Gb of memory for the rumen dataset.
source: The complete M2M workflow ran in 81 min on a cluster with 72 CPUs and 144 Gb of memory.
evidence: This is stated as a performance metric for the tool on the rumen dataset.

claim: GSMNs of the cow rumen MAGs dataset consisted in average of 1155 (±199) reactions and 1422 (±212) metabolites.
source: GSMNs of the cow rumen MAGs dataset consisted in average of 1155 (±199) reactions and 1422 (±212) metabolites.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the GSMN reconstruction for the rumen dataset.

claim: 73.8% of the reactions in the rumen GSMNs could be associated to genes.
source: 73.8% of the reactions could be associated to genes.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the GSMN reconstruction for the rumen dataset.

claim: The distributions of the numbers of reactions, pathways, metabolites and genes are very similar for both gut and rumen datasets.
source: Altogether, these distributions are very similar for both datasets although the initial number of genes in the whole genomes varies a lot (Appendix 1 g), a difference that is expected between MAGs and reference genomes.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the comparison and refers to Appendix 1.

claim: The average number of reactions per GSMN is slightly higher for the MAGs of the rumen than for the reference genomes of the gut.
source: Interestingly, the average number of reactions per GSMN is slightly higher for the MAGs of the rumen than for the reference genomes of the gut.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the comparison.

claim: The 913 rumen MAGs exhibited a CheckM completeness score between 80% and 100% (average: 90.61%, standard deviation: 5.26%, median: 91.03%).
source: This is consistent with the high-quality scores of the MAGs described in the original publication: the 913 MAGs exhibited a CheckM (Parks et al., 2015) completeness score between 80% and 100% (average: 90.61%, standard deviation: 5.26%, median: 91.03%) (Stewart et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Parks et al., 2015 and Stewart et al., 2018.

claim: A cooperation potential of 296 metabolic end-products only reachable through the community was identified for the rumen dataset.
source: We identified a cooperation potential of 296 metabolic end-products only reachable through the community.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the analysis on the rumen dataset.

claim: The minimal community for the rumen dataset consisted of 44 GSMNs.
source: The minimal community consisted of 44 GSMNs, sufficient to produce all metabolites reachable through cooperation in the initial community composition.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the community reduction on the rumen dataset.

claim: 127 key species were identified for the rumen dataset, consisting of 20 essential symbionts and 107 alternative ones.
source: These could be described through 127 key species, consisting of 20 essential symbionts and 107 alternative ones.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the community reduction on the rumen dataset.

claim: The global set of producible metabolites in the community and the contents of the metabolic cooperation potential remain stable between degraded and original rumen datasets.
source: The global set of producible metabolites in the community and the contents of the metabolic cooperation potential remain stable between datasets.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the degradation experiment.

claim: A single subset of 36 metabolites is only reachable by the original rumen dataset.
source: In both we observe a single subset of 36 metabolites that is only reachable by the original dataset.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the degradation experiment.

claim: Producibility analyses and community selections performed by M2M are stable to small genome degradations of up to 2% of random gene loss in all genomes or 5% in 80% of the genomes.
source: However, producibility analyses and community selections performed by M2M are stable to small genome degradations of up to 2% of random gene loss in all genomes or 5% in 80% of the genomes.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the degradation experiment.

claim: The criteria typically used for MAG quality (>80% completeness, <10% degradation) are likely sufficient to get a coarse-grained, yet valuable first picture of the metabolism.
source: The criteria typically used for MAG quality (>80% completeness, <10% degradation) are likely sufficient to get a coarse-grained, yet valuable first picture of the metabolism.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the degradation experiment.

claim: The robustness in M2M algorithms could be explained by the reported stability of the network expansion algorithm to missing reactions.
source: This robustness in our algorithms could be explained by the fact that (i) missing genes in degraded MAGs may not be related to metabolism, (ii) by the reported stability of the network expansion algorithm to missing reactions (Handorf et al., 2005), and (iii) by the fact that multiple genes can be associated to the same metabolic reaction (redundancy in pathway representation).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Handorf et al., 2005 and stated as a possible explanation.

claim: Multiple genes can be associated to the same metabolic reaction (redundancy in pathway representation).
source: This robustness in our algorithms could be explained by the fact that (i) missing genes in degraded MAGs may not be related to metabolism, (ii) by the reported stability of the network expansion algorithm to missing reactions (Handorf et al., 2005), and (iii) by the fact that multiple genes can be associated to the same metabolic reaction (redundancy in pathway representation).
evidence: This is stated as a possible explanation for robustness.

claim: A total of 778 MGS were retrieved from the diabetes dataset and used to build GSMNs.
source: A total of 778 MGS were retrieved from the dataset and used to build GSMNs (Table 2), whereas when using the mapping of OTUs to existing curated GSMNs, only 289 GSMNs were used.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the dataset and presented in Table 2.

claim: When using the mapping of OTUs to existing curated GSMNs, only 289 GSMNs were used for the diabetes dataset.
source: A total of 778 MGS were retrieved from the dataset and used to build GSMNs (Table 2), whereas when using the mapping of OTUs to existing curated GSMNs, only 289 GSMNs were used.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the dataset and presented in Table 2.

claim: In average, communities in the diabetes dataset were composed of 108 (±29) GSMNs.
source: In average, communities were composed of 108 (±29) GSMNs.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the analysis on the diabetes dataset.

claim: The median community size for the diabetes dataset was 111.
source: The median community size was 111 (Supplementary file 1 - Table 20).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the analysis on the diabetes dataset.

claim: The effect of the cohort (MHD, SWE) was strong in the analyses performed with MGS.
source: The effect of the cohort (MHD, SWE) was strong in the analyses performed with MGS, impacting community sizes, size and composition (in families of metabolites) of the set of metabolites producible by the community, as well as the cooperation potential.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the analysis on the diabetes dataset.

claim: A classification experiment using the composition of the community scope or the composition of the cooperation potential can efficiently determine the cohort of the samples.
source: A classification experiment using the composition of the community scope or the composition of the cooperation potential can efficiently determine the cohort of the samples (Appendix 2—figure 3 panels c and g).
evidence: This is stated as a result and refers to Appendix 2—figure 3.

claim: Similar differences between cohorts were also observed in Diener et al., 2020 and in Forslund et al., 2015 based on functional or taxonomic annotations.
source: Similar differences between cohorts were also observed in Diener et al., 2020 and in Forslund et al., 2015 based on functional or taxonomic annotations, likely driven by the different sampling protocols used in the two datasets (Forslund et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Diener et al., 2020 and Forslund et al., 2015.

claim: The community diversity varied between disease statuses, with a significantly higher number of MGS observed in T1D individuals forming the initial communities.
source: The community diversity varied between disease statuses, with a significantly higher number of MGS observed in T1D individuals forming the initial communities (anova F(2,112) = 8.346, p<0.01, eta-squared = 0.13, Tukey HSD test p<0.01 vs control).
evidence: This is stated as a result with statistical support.

claim: The higher diversity for diseased individuals is reflected at the metabolic level through the putative producibility of a wider set of metabolites for T1D.
source: We observe that the distribution of the community sizes is broader for control individuals. The higher diversity for diseased individuals is reflected at the metabolic level through the putative producibility of a wider set of metabolites for T1D (anova F(2,112) = 6.606, p<0.01, eta-squared = 0.11, Tukey HSD p<0.01 vs control) and to a lesser extent for T2D communities (Tukey HSD p=0.05 vs control).
evidence: This is stated as a result with statistical support.

claim: The putative producibility of some families of metabolites (alcohols, esters, carbohydrates, amino acids, acids) in the community scopes differed between metabolic communities derived from diseased and healthy individuals.
source: The putative producibility of some families of metabolites (alcohols, esters, carbohydrates, amino acids, acids) in the community scopes also differed between metabolic communities derived from diseased and healthy individuals (anova p<0.05), whereas other metabolic families like lipids remained stable between cohorts.
evidence: This is stated as a result with statistical support.

claim: A classification experiment on the composition of the community scope can, to some extent (AUC = 0.75 ± 0.15), decipher between healthy or diabetes statuses.
source: A classification experiment on the composition of the community scope can, to some extent (AUC = 0.75 ± 0.15), decipher between healthy or diabetes statuses (Figure 4d) but classification between T1D and T2D was not achievable (Appendix 2—figure 4).
evidence: This is stated as a result and shown in Figure 4d.

claim: Classification between T1D and T2D was not achievable using community scope composition.
source: A classification experiment on the composition of the community scope can, to some extent (AUC = 0.75 ± 0.15), decipher between healthy or diabetes statuses (Figure 4d) but classification between T1D and T2D was not achievable (Appendix 2—figure 4).
evidence: This is stated as a result and refers to Appendix 2—figure 4.

claim: A small number of MGS (N = 11) GSMNs were predicted to be able to individually produce butyrate from the nutrients in the diabetes dataset.
source: A small number of MGS (N = 11) GSMNs were predicted to be able to individually produce butyrate from the nutrients.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the SCFA analysis on the diabetes dataset.

claim: All 778 MGS were capable to ferment acetate.
source: All 778 MGS were capable to ferment acetate and most of them propionate (N = 515).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the SCFA analysis on the diabetes dataset.

claim: Most MGS (N = 515) were capable to ferment propionate.
source: All 778 MGS were capable to ferment acetate and most of them propionate (N = 515).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the SCFA analysis on the diabetes dataset.

claim: The putative production of butyrate in the 170 communities when allowing cooperation between GSMNs was systematic.
source: The putative production of butyrate in the 170 communities when allowing cooperation between GSMNs was systematic.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the SCFA analysis on the diabetes dataset.

claim: A majority (54.1%) of the unique MGS predicted as possible butyrate producers in communities belonged to the Firmicutes phylum.
source: As expected (Rivière et al., 2016), a majority (54.1%) of the unique MGS predicted as possible butyrate producers in communities (GSMNs comprising a reaction producing butyrate that could be activated in a community) belonged to the Firmicutes phylum.
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by a citation to Rivière et al., 2016.

claim: In 62.6% of cases, the putative butyrate producers observed in the communities were Firmicutes.
source: Altogether, in 62.6% of cases, the putative butyrate producers observed in the communities were Firmicutes.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the SCFA analysis on the diabetes dataset.

claim: The number of putative butyrate producers in communities was significantly higher in T1D individuals compared to control and T2D.
source: We compared the number of putative butyrate producers in communities from MHD samples according to the disease status of the individuals. Their number was significantly higher in the communities of T1D individuals compared to control and T2D (anova F(2,111) = 9.27, p<0.01, eta-squared = 0.14, and Tukey HSD test p<0.01 vs control and p=0.02 vs T2D) which could be explained by the higher MGS diversity observed in T1D communities compared to the others.
evidence: This is stated as a result with statistical support.

claim: M2M is a new software system for the functional analysis of metagenomic datasets at the metabolic level.
source: M2M is a new software system for the functional analysis of metagenomic datasets at the metabolic level.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: M2M can be used as an all-in-one pipeline or as independent steps in order to depict an initial picture of metabolic complementarity within a community.
source: M2M can be used as an all-in-one pipeline or as independent steps in order to depict an initial picture of metabolic complementarity within a community.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Metabolic networks reconstructed from reference genomes and MAGs display similar characteristics.
source: We showed that metabolic networks reconstructed from reference genomes and MAGs display similar characteristics and that M2M modelling predictions are robust to missing genes in the original genomes.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section.

claim: M2M modelling predictions are robust to missing genes in the original genomes.
source: We showed that metabolic networks reconstructed from reference genomes and MAGs display similar characteristics and that M2M modelling predictions are robust to missing genes in the original genomes.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section.

claim: Application to real metagenomic samples of individuals demonstrated that qualitative modelling of metabolism retrieves known features from metagenomics and quantitative modelling analyses.
source: Finally, application to real metagenomic samples of individuals demonstrated that qualitative modelling of metabolism retrieves known features from metagenomics and quantitative modelling analyses.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section.

claim: M2M provides a first order analysis with a minimal cost in terms of required data and computational effort.
source: M2M provides a first order analysis with a minimal cost in terms of required data and computational effort.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section.

claim: The identification of alternative and essential symbionts by M2M is an additional solution to help identify critical species.
source: The identification of alternative and essential symbionts by M2M is an additional solution to help identify these critical species.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Essential symbionts are close to the concept of keystone species as they are predicted to have a role in every minimal community associated to a function.
source: In particular, essential symbionts are close to the concept of keystone species as they are predicted to have a role in every minimal community associated to a function.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Network expansion enables the calculation of the scope of one or several metabolic networks in given nutritional conditions.
source: Network expansion enables the calculation of the scope of one or several metabolic networks in given nutritional conditions, described as seed compounds.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the method.

claim: Network expansion has been widely used to analyse and refine metabolic networks.
source: Network expansion has been widely used to analyse and refine metabolic networks (Matthäus et al., 2008; Laniau et al., 2017; Christian et al., 2009; Prigent et al., 2017), including for microbiota analysis (Christian et al., 2007; Ofaim et al., 2017; Opatovsky et al., 2018; Frioux et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Network expansion is a complementary alternative to quantitative constraint-based methods such as flux balance analysis.
source: Network expansion is a complementary alternative to quantitative constraint-based methods (Ebenhöh et al., 2004; Handorf et al., 2005) such as flux balance analysis as it does not require biomass reactions nor accurate stoichiometry.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ebenhöh et al., 2004 and Handorf et al., 2005.

claim: Network expansion does not require biomass reactions nor accurate stoichiometry.
source: Network expansion is a complementary alternative to quantitative constraint-based methods (Ebenhöh et al., 2004; Handorf et al., 2005) such as flux balance analysis as it does not require biomass reactions nor accurate stoichiometry.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the method.

claim: The network expansion algorithm offers a good trade-off between the accuracy of metabolic predictions and the precision required for the input data.
source: This algorithm offers a good trade-off between the accuracy of metabolic predictions and the precision required for the input data, adapted to the challenges in studying non-model organisms and their likely incomplete models of metabolism (Bernstein et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Bernstein et al., 2019.

claim: Answer Set Programming can easily scale the analysis of minimal communities among thousands of networks considered in interaction.
source: Answer Set Programming can easily scale the analysis of minimal communities among thousands of networks considered in interaction and ensures with efficient solving heuristics that the whole space of solutions is parsed to retrieve key species for chosen end-products.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the method.

claim: The relevance of MiSCoTo has been recently experimentally demonstrated.
source: The relevance of MiSCoTo (Frioux et al., 2018), the algorithm for minimal community selection used in M2M, has been recently experimentally demonstrated.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Frioux et al., 2018.

claim: MiSCoTo was applied to design bacterial communities to support the growth of a brown alga in nearly axenic conditions.
source: It was applied to design bacterial communities to support the growth of a brown alga in nearly axenic conditions (Burgunter-Delamare et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Burgunter-Delamare et al., 2019.

claim: The inoculated algae exhibited a significant increase in growth and metabolic profiles that at least partially aligned with the predictions.
source: Despite the difficulty inherent to controlling the communities for a complex alga, the inoculated algae exhibited a significant increase in growth and metabolic profiles that at least partially aligned with the predictions, demonstrating the versatility in application fields of our methods.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experimental validation.

claim: One challenge in applying M2M is to accurately estimate the nutrients available in a given environment (seeds).
source: One challenge in applying our tool is to accurately estimate the nutrients available in a given environment (seeds), on which the computation of network expansion relies.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the Discussion section.

claim: Network expansion has been shown to be sensitive to cycles in GSMNs.
source: However, network expansion has been shown to be sensitive to cycles in GSMNs and it is therefore relevant to include some cofactors (or currency metabolites e.g. ADP) in the seeds to activate such cycles, the way many studies proceed (Cottret et al., 2010; Greenblum et al., 2012; Eng and Borenstein, 2016; Julien-Laferrière et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The cost of exchanges or their number are not taken into account in M2M.
source: In addition, it has to be noted that the cost of exchanges or their number are not taken into account in M2M.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the Discussion section.

claim: Transport reactions are hardly recovered by automatic methods.
source: Transport reactions are hardly recovered by automatic methods (Bernstein et al., 2019) and validation of cross-feedings implies an additional work on transporters identification.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Bernstein et al., 2019.

claim: Considering the presence/absence of MGS might lead to overestimate the production of some metabolites.
source: Considering the presence/absence of MGS might lead to overestimate the production of some metabolites.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the Discussion section.

claim: M2M infers phenotypes directly from genotypes, thereby ignoring the possible non-expression of metabolic-related genes in specific conditions and the regulation of those genes.
source: In addition, we infer phenotypes directly from genotypes, thereby ignoring the possible non-expression of metabolic-related genes in specific conditions and the regulation of those genes.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the Discussion section.

claim: The number of curated GSMNs for species found in microbiotas increases.
source: The number of curated GSMNs for species found in microbiotas increases (Magnúsdóttir et al., 2017), constituting a highly valuable resource for the study of interactions by mapping metagenomic data or OTUs to the taxonomy of genomes associated to these GSMNs.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Magnúsdóttir et al., 2017.

claim: The proportion of reads that are not mapped to a genome with an associated GSMN can be very high.
source: Yet, the variety of (reference) genomes obtained from shotgun metagenomic experiments is such than species and strains may not belong to the ones for which a curated GSMN is available. In that case, the proportion of reads that are not mapped to a genome with an associated GSMN can be very high (Diener et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Diener et al., 2020.

claim: Predictions from GSMN mapping can be misleading as genomes vary a lot between genera, species, and even strains, and so can the metabolism.
source: In addition, predictions from GSMN mapping can be misleading as it is known that genomes vary a lot between genera, species, and even strains, (Ansorge et al., 2019) and so can the metabolism.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ansorge et al., 2019.

claim: Recent methods for assembling genomes directly from metagenomes lead to nearly complete genomes for possibly unknown species.
source: Recent methods for assembling genomes directly from metagenomes lead to nearly complete genomes for possibly unknown species on which one may still want to get metabolic insights (Almeida et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Almeida et al., 2019.

claim: Long-reads sequencing associated with short-reads sequencing can give access to complete microbial genomes.
source: Long-reads sequencing associated with short-reads sequencing can also give access to complete microbial genomes (Moss et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Moss et al., 2020.

claim: Single-cell methods can be useful for the acquisition of genomes and metagenomes.
source: Finally, single-cell methods can be useful for the acquisition of genomes and metagenomes (Treitli et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Treitli et al., 2019.

claim: M2M answers to the need for de novo metabolic inference and screening.
source: M2M answers to the need for de novo metabolic inference and screening, which is likely to become a routine in the rapidly evolving context of microbiota genome sequencing.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section.

claim: M2M allows metabolic modelling of large-scale communities, based on reference genomes or de novo constructed MAGs.
source: M2M allows metabolic modelling of large-scale communities, based on reference genomes or de novo constructed MAGs, inferring metabolic complementarity found within communities.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Conclusion section.

claim: M2M is a flexible framework that automates GSMN reconstruction, individually and collectively analyse GSMNs, and performs community selection for targeted functions.
source: M2M is a flexible framework that automates GSMN reconstruction, individually and collectively analyse GSMNs, and performs community selection for targeted functions.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Conclusion section.

claim: The large combinatorics of minimal communities due to functional redundancy in microbiotas is addressed by providing key species associated to metabolic end-products.
source: The large combinatorics of minimal communities due to functional redundancy in microbiotas is addressed by providing key species associated to metabolic end-products.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Conclusion section.

claim: M2M is robust against the uncertainty inherent to metagenomics data.
source: Our method is robust against the uncertainty inherent to metagenomics data.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Conclusion section.

claim: M2M scales to typical microbial communities found in the gut.
source: It scales to typical microbial communities found in the gut and predicts key species for functions of interest at the metabolic level.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Conclusion section.

claim: M2M predicts key species for functions of interest at the metabolic level.
source: It scales to typical microbial communities found in the gut and predicts key species for functions of interest at the metabolic level.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Conclusion section.

claim: M2M is an answer to the need for scalable predictive methods in the context of metagenomics where the number of available genomes continues to rise.
source: This software is an answer to the need for scalable predictive methods in the context of metagenomics where the number of available genomes continues to rise.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Conclusion section.
